about: compiler/nativeobj: the Ergo producer of a Go archive (route C, NATIVE-OBJECT-ROUNDTRIP). Each row breaks one contract of the archive; the law that holds that contract (verify.ergo, slots.ergo) kills it through the independent decoders, and the round trip (ergo run ./cmd/nativeobj -- verify --seed 17) is the behavioural witness. Under CRUNCH (common.md, rule 2) the rows are named, not run: origin says not-run-crunch. Paths are from the repository root.

mutants.name: wrong-pkgdef-fingerprint
mutants.rule: The export data ends with the first 8 bytes of its SHA-256, and the object header carries the same fingerprint (the linker compares it with every importer's record).

mutants.name: own-archive-member-missing
mutants.rule: The archive holds both members the producer wrote, __.PKGDEF then _go_.o; neither is left to a stock tool.

mutants.name: wrong-abi-arg
mutants.rule: ABIInternal passes integer argument k in the k-th of RAX, RBX, RCX, RDI, RSI, R8..R11; the prologue takes parameter k from it.

mutants.name: live-slot-unmarked
mutants.rule: At each call the locals pointer map marks every pointer slot live across it, so the GC keeps its object and the stack copier moves a stack pointer.

mutants.name: wrong-safe-pc
mutants.rule: The stack-map index at a call's return address minus one names that call's own map.

mutants.name: missing-pointer-barrier
mutants.rule: A heap pointer store runs the write barrier whenever runtime.writeBarrier is set.

mutants.name: reloc-target-swapped
mutants.rule: Each relocation names the symbol its instruction calls or reads.

mutants.name: init-double-run
mutants.rule: The inittask lists each init function once, so the runtime runs it once.
